organization: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR)
title: Find a Licensed Roofer (consumer brochure)
claim: Two Illinois roofing license types (limited = residential and condo buildings of up to 8 units; unlimited = residential, commercial, industrial); subcontracted roofing must also be done by a licensed roofer; contracts over $1,000 require the Home Repair consumer-rights brochure; contractors may not rebate insurance deductibles or represent homeowners on insurance claims.
excerpt: If a general contractor has to sub out the work to a subcontractor, the subcontractor must also be licensed as a roofer.
limitations: Consumer brochure, not the statute; printed 7-23. Does not state bond or insurance dollar amounts.

title: Roofing Contractor, Licensed (profession page)
claim: IDFPR licenses roofing contractors; licensure runs through a designated qualifying party who must pass the Roofing Contractor Qualifying Party Examination (Continental Testing Services).
excerpt: Page lists 'Roofing Contractor Qualifying Party Examination' and qualifying-party designation/termination forms (f1919rf, f1920rf).
limitations: Page lists forms only; fees, experience requirements and insurance amounts not stated on the page itself.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (ILCS) / JCAR (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1460)
title: 225 ILCS 335/3 Roofing Industry Licensing Act - Application for license; 68 IAC 1460 bonding rule
claim: Roofing license applicants must post a continuous surety bond of $10,000 (limited license) or $25,000 (unlimited license) and carry public liability and property damage insurance in amounts set by IDFPR.
excerpt: continuous bond to the Department in the amount of $10,000 for a limited license and in the amount of $25,000 for an unlimited license
limitations: Text obtained via search-result excerpts of ilga.gov and the JCAR rule; ilga.gov returned HTTP 503/TLS failure on direct fetch 2026-11-28. Search excerpt showed Section 3 marked 'scheduled to be repealed January 1, 2026' (sunset); whether the Act was extended is UNVERIFIED. Insurance dollar amounts not confirmed.

organization: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
title: General Contractor License
claim: Chicago GC license required for most construction/alteration/repair incl. work exempt from building permit under Sec. 402; classes: A unlimited/$5M ins/$3,500; B $20M/$3M/$1,800; C $10M/$2M/$1,300; D $4M/$2M/$900; E $500k/$1M/$300. Subs under a licensed GC's supervision need no own GC license; licensed mason/electrical/plumbing contractors exempt within scope. Application needs financial-solvency statement, B+ rated insurer; no exam listed. GCs must follow home-repair consumer rules on residential work.
excerpt: Class E General Contractor $500,000 none $1 million per occurrence ... Class E $300.00 $300.00
limitations: Licensing guidance page; Municipal Code controls. Fetched via curl (WebFetch got 403). Insurance increases for C/D effective 2026-01-01.

organization: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
title: Mason Contractor License
claim: Chicago mason contractor license required for stone/concrete/brick/terra cotta work in buildings above or below ground; exceptions include sidewalks, paving, foundations for fences/decks/open porches; business must employ a 'supervising mason' who passed a City written exam (age 21+); exam $150, license $150/yr; mason work must be done by W-2 employees, not independent contractors.
excerpt: a business must employ at least one individual who has passed a written mason examination (a 'supervising mason')
limitations: Guidance page; Chapter 4-376 controls. Exam pass rates and experience prerequisites (if any) not stated.

organization: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
title: Electrical Contractor License
claim: Chicago electrical contractor license (with licensed supervising electrician) required for any wiring incl. signaling, communication and alarm systems, whether or not a permit is required; exception for State-licensed private alarm contractors (must register with City); no 1099 electricians.
excerpt: This includes electrical, lighting, communication, and alarm systems and equipment.
limitations: Supervising-electrician exam requirements not captured in excerpt.

organization: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
title: Plumbing Contractor License
claim: A City of Chicago plumbing contractor license is required for water supply and sanitary drainage piping, even for contractors already licensed by the State; licensed plumbing contractors may also do drain-layer work.
excerpt: A plumbing contractor licensed by the State of Illinois must also obtain a City of Chicago plumbing contractor license
limitations: Did not capture license fee or examination detail.

title: Building Permit Professional License Lookup - Help
claim: Expediters are individuals licensed by Chicago BACP and must be associated with a licensed expediter company as employee or owner.
excerpt: Expediters must be associated with a licensed expediter company, either as an employee or owner.
limitations: Help page; does not state fees or exam.

title: RFP: Permit Expediter Professional Services (PS3011), incl. Exhibit J (MCC 4-6-250/4-6-260)
claim: Reproduces Chicago Municipal Code 4-6-250: expediter = anyone paid to prepare/submit/monitor permit applications; exemptions for licensed architects/engineers/attorneys, owner/tenant salaried employees, the GC and licensed trade contractor; licensees need fingerprinting, $300,000 per-occurrence CGL naming the City, no fraud/bribery convictions, age 18+. A sample PBC task order shows a not-to-exceed $350 fee for basic permit-application services; contract term 3 yrs + two 1-yr options.
excerpt: The value of this Task Order is an amount not to-exceed fee of $350.00 for Basic Services
limitations: 2018 document; Code text and fee levels may have changed. $350 is a public-owner basic-service task order, not a market price for private plan-based permits.

title: Building Permits dataset (analyst SoQL queries)
claim: Issued permits: 48,540 (2019), 38,335 (2022), 32,032 (2025), 29,067 (2026 to ~Nov 27). 2025 by type: express 20,427; renovation/alteration 5,505; new construction 1,460; wrecking 661. 6,428 of 2025 permits list an expediter among contacts 1-6 (reno/alt 2,567; new 424; express 3,272); 204 distinct expediter names, top-10 hold 46.3%, 34 with >=50 permits. Keyword counts 2025: ROOF 4,955; TUCKPOINT 1,804; PORCH 1,623; ADU 78; COACH HOUSE 87. Express-permit median reported cost: roof $22,158 (n=4,058), tuckpointing $15,000 (n=1,779), porch $10,000 (n=473).
excerpt: Analyst queries of official permit records (e.g., 2025 issued permits = 32,032; expediter-listed = 6,428).
limitations: Analyst-computed; keyword matching on free-text work descriptions is approximate; reported_cost is applicant-declared; only contact fields 1-6 searched for expediter role; names aggregated as written.

title: Building Violations dataset (analyst SoQL queries)
